Prefer the biggest story you have a real angle on: a bigger story reaches more people, but a forced angle on it loses to a true one on a smaller one. At least 2 of the top 3 in your ranking have a hook. When a story on the list is about a public figure, at least one pitch is a roast: it goes at them by name, hard and rude, for the public thing the story says they did (shape "roast"). ## The reel service

`hands/reel` renders clips and songs on the `reel` service
(docs/hands.md, "reel"). It is opt-in, behind the `reel` profile, and posts
nothing. It needs about 4 cores and 4 GB while rendering (capped at that in
compose; one render at a time). To start it on the box:

```sh
git submodule update --init vendor/moneyprinter        # the pinned release tag
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile reel build reel
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile reel up -d reel
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine curl -fsS http://reel:8080/ping   # "pong"
```

`up -d reel` starts that one service; it does not recreate the spine. Then
check what a clip would be, with nothing rendered:

```sh
echo '{"kind":"clip","script":"...","materials":["brain/assets/tiny/tiny-love.jpg"]}' |
  docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine env DRY_RUN=1 hands/reel make
```

`REEL_URL` defaults to `http://reel:8080`. The caps (`REEL_MAX_PER_DAY`,
`REEL_SONGS_MAX_PER_WEEK`) and the music switch (`REEL_MUSIC`, off) are in
`secrets/teeny.env` (`deploy/teeny.env.example`). Renders wait in the
`reel-storage` volume until the hand copies them into `state/media/` and
deletes the task; a restart of the service forgets its tasks, and a folder
left by a task in flight then stays in the volume
(`docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile reel down reel` and
`docker volume rm teeny-spine_reel-storage` clear it).

Egress: the only outbound call the service makes is upstream's Edge TTS
request (`speech.platform.bing.com`, Microsoft's unofficial endpoint, over
https). No model, stock library, upload service or update check is
configured or run. Compose does not restrict it today: the service sits on
the stack's default network, which reaches the internet. To hold it to that
one host, either put `reel` on its own network with an egress proxy that
allows only `speech.platform.bing.com:443` (set `HTTPS_PROXY` on the
service; edge-tts honours it), or add a host firewall rule on the
`DOCKER-USER` chain that drops the reel container's traffic to anything but
that host. Either way the spine still reaches it on the compose network.

To move the pin: check out the new release tag in `vendor/moneyprinter`, run
`python3 -m unittest discover -s hands/tests -t hands/tests -p 'test_reel.py'`
(its schema check reads the new job model), rebuild, render one clip, and
land it as a pull request. Never edit the submodule; a fix upstream needs is
a pull request to `harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo`.

`hands/meme templates` and `hands/meme template` render known meme templates
on the `memegen` service (docs/hands.md, "meme"). Opt-in, behind the

```sh
git submodule update --init vendor/memegen              # the pinned commit
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile memegen build memegen
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile memegen up -d memegen
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine hands/meme templates --max 3
```

`up -d memegen` starts that one service; it does not recreate the spine.
Then render one with nothing saved:

```sh
echo '{"template":"drake","lines":["a","b"],"teeny":"brain/assets/tiny/tiny-love.jpg"}' |
  docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine env DRY_RUN=1 hands/meme template
```

`MEMEGEN_URL` defaults to `http://memegen:5000`. The studio drafts memes
only when `STUDIO_FORMATS` names `meme` (`deploy/teeny.env.example`).

The image is upstream's own build (`python:3.13` bookworm with poetry,
about 2.6 GB). What runs is `deploy/memegen/front.py`, mounted read-only:

(mounted read-only at `/teeny`, named `http://teeny-art/...`) and every other

it from fetching. The service writes only inside its container (each
template folder caches the pictures pasted into it, `images/` each render),
so it is not `read_only`; recreating it starts it clean.

To move the pin: upstream tags no releases, so pick a commit on `main` whose
CI passed, check it out in `vendor/memegen`, run
`python3 -m unittest discover -s hands/tests -t hands/tests -p 'test_templates.py'`
(it checks that what the front replaces is still upstream's), rebuild,
render one, and land it as a pull request. Never edit the submodule.

## The ingest service

`hands/remake` studies short videos on the `ingest` service
(docs/hands.md, "remake"): a pinned `yt-dlp` and `ffmpeg` behind
`deploy/ingest/serve.py`. Opt-in, behind the `ingest` profile; it posts and
spends nothing. It holds no key and mounts nothing of Teeny's; its only
setting is an optional proxy for YouTube. To start it on the box:

```sh
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile ingest build ingest
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile ingest up -d ingest
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine curl -fsS http://ingest:8090/ping
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine hands/remake charts --max 3
```

`up -d ingest` starts that one service; it does not recreate the spine.
`INGEST_URL` defaults to `http://ingest:8090`. Which charts it reads is
`REMAKE_TIKTOK_ACCOUNTS` and `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` (`deploy/teeny.env.example`);
with neither set, `charts` answers nothing and says both are off.

YouTube answers this box's address "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" for
every player client (2026-11-20), so YouTube videos need a proxy: copy
`deploy/ingest.env.example` to `secrets/ingest.env`, set `INGEST_PROXY_URL`,
and recreate the service. The proxy URL is read by that container only; the
service takes it out of every error it reports. TikTok video downloads and
account listings work without one; TikTok's tag and trending pages do not.

The image is `python:3.11-slim` (the reel image's digest) with ffmpeg and
yt-dlp installed from its release wheel by hash: `YTDLP_VERSION` and
`YTDLP_SHA256` in `deploy/ingest.Dockerfile` move together (the digest is the
wheel's sha256 on PyPI). yt-dlp changes often to keep up with the sites, so
when a site stops working, bump both, rebuild and recreate. The service runs
as its own user with a read-only root, a 256 MB tmpfs, no capabilities, no
new privileges, 2 CPUs, 2 GB and 256 processes, and no published port.
Fetches live in the `ingest-storage` volume until `hands/remake` deletes them;
the service also sweeps any older than an hour (`INGEST_REAP_MINUTES`), and
at start everything left from an earlier run. It is on a network of its own (`ingest-net`, shared only with cortexdb, whose namespace the spine lives in, so the spine still reaches `http://ingest:8090`): what it fetches cannot reach reel, memegen, xhook or the web page. Adding that network recreates cortexdb, and so the spine, the first time it is deployed. yt-dlp runs only the YouTube, TikTok and Instagram extractors, never `generic`. One job at a time: a second is
answered 429. Compose does not restrict egress at the network level (as for
`reel`): what keeps it from fetching anything but video pages is the address
allowlist in `deploy/ingest/policy.py`, which `python3 -m unittest discover -s
hands/tests -t hands/tests -p 'test_policy.py'` pins.

## The studio cutover

Merging and deploying the studio changes what Teeny posts in public: from the
first slot after the restart, every original post on X is written by
`bin/studio` (docs/architecture.md, §4b) and goes out with no per-post
approval. Replies are unchanged. To deploy it:

1. Pull, with the submodules:

   ```sh
   git -C /home/ubuntu/teeny pull --ff-only
   git -C /home/ubuntu/teeny submodule update --init --recursive
   ```
2. Add these lines to `secrets/teeny.env` (the rest of the `STUDIO_*`
   switches can stay at their defaults; `deploy/teeny.env.example` shows
   these commented out, so a copy of it stays off). `STUDIO` takes only
   `1/true/yes/on` or `0/false/no/off`: anything else posts nothing on either
   path and fails `bin/doctor`:

   ```sh
   STUDIO=1
   STUDIO_WRITER_MODEL=claude-fable-5.2
   STUDIO_EDITOR_MODEL=claude-opus-5.5
   SAFETY_JUDGE_MODEL=claude-opus-5.5
   ```

   `SAFETY_JUDGE_MODEL` is what the truth judge, the cold reader, the anchor
   judge and the guard's content judge ask, so no judge is the writer. It is
   also asked for every reply and every Moltbook write the guard screens
   (and with it unset, or equal to the writer's model, a live slot posts
   nothing: `bin/doctor` warns):
   expect the judge's share of the model bill to grow. Leave `STUDIO_DRY`
   unset (0): set to 1, every slot runs its gates and posts nothing.
3. Check no generation is running, since a restart kills it:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f /home/ubuntu/teeny/deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine bin/evolve status | jq .running
   ```

   Go on only when it prints `false`.
4. Rebuild the spine image and start it (the cron jobs are reconciled at
   boot):

   ```sh
   docker compose -f /home/ubuntu/teeny/deploy/compose.yaml up -d --build spine
   ```
5. Verify, after boot:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f /home/ubuntu/teeny/deploy/compose.yaml logs spine | grep "the studio's"
   ```

   must show `model: the studio's claude-fable-5.2 has a N-token window` and
   the same for `claude-opus-5.5` (bin/lib/model_windows.sh). A line saying
   "no window" or "refused a window" means its turns may come back empty: fix
   that before the next slot (a model set later, or for one run, gets its
   window from `bin/ask --model` on its first turn; `bin/doctor --live`'s
   `studio models answer` asks each studio model one turn and fails on a
   refusal). Then `bin/crons` lists `teeny.studio-0430`,
   `-0930`, `-1500`, `-sunday` and `-2300` and no `teeny.x-quote`,
   `teeny.morning`, `teeny.take`, `teeny.show` or `teeny.growth`; `bin/doctor
   --live` is green; and a preview that posts nothing:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f /home/ubuntu/teeny/deploy/compose.yaml exec -T spine bin/studio --dry-run --slot check
   ```

   After the first slot: `tail state/studio/<slot>.log` (the detached run's
   output), `hands/story runs --limit 4` (every run, its pick,

**To roll back**, set `STUDIO=0` in `secrets/teeny.env` and restart the
spine (step 3 first). Nothing else changes: each studio job then runs its
slot's old playbook (x-quote, morning, take, growth on Sundays, show),
`shiplog` runs again at 23:10, the mind's `post_x` posts, and the brief and
the peer quote post without the editor. The schedule is the same, except
that the brief runs at 14:55 and 22:55 (five minutes before the slot, not
after).

- For a script or the brain, pull, then restart. Nothing of Teeny's is
  baked into the image. `brain/MEMORY.md` is Teeny's live page and not in
  git, so a pull never touches it; the repository keeps where it started,
  `brain/MEMORY.seed.md`, and the boot starts the live page from it when
  there is none.

  refuses (Teeny has rewritten the page since). Move the page aside, pull,
  and put it back, where it is now ignored
  (`bin/test/memory_page_test.sh` checks these steps):

  agent's browser profile is in `state/browser/profile/` and its downloads in
  `state/browser/downloads/`, so a logged-in session survives restarts.

  `hands/tasks list`. `hands/tasks list --status needs_human` is what the

## Backups

Back up `brain/storage.db` and `secrets/openhuman.key` together.
`storage.db` holds all of the core's state, including the cron jobs and its
secrets, which are encrypted under that key. A database without its key has
unreadable secrets, and a key without the database has nothing to unlock.

`state/hands.db` holds the hands' ledgers and queues. Back it up too.

# Tiny Drops: the diary contract

The giveaway hand (`hands/giveaway`) publishes every round to the public diary
repository (`teenydroid/diary`) under `giveaways/`. The `/rewards` page reads
those files and nothing else from Teeny's side. This document and the types in
`web/src/lib/drops.ts` describe the same contract, so change them together.

The page treats the repository as public input. It checks every field again,
and it does not show a round whose file doesn't parse. It never fills a gap
with a default number.

## `giveaways/index.json`

```json
{ "rounds": [ { "id": 3, "tag": "drop #3", "status": "open", "deadline": "2026-11-20T18:00:00Z" } ] }
```

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer ≥ 1 | unique |
| `tag` | string | exactly `"drop #<id>"` |
| `status` | `"open"` \| `"drawn"` \| `"settled"` \| `"clawed_back"` | |
| `deadline` | ISO 8601 UTC | |

The page reads the newest 12 rounds.

## `giveaways/drop-<id>.json`

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id`, `tag`, `status`, `deadline` | as in the index | |
| `format` | `"drop"` \| `"milestone"` \| `"challenge"` | |
| `pool_tiny` | decimal string, whole $TINY (`"250000"`, `"1234.5"`) | no more fractional digits than `decimals` |
| `winners` | integer | how many random winners |
| `best_reply_tiny` | decimal string | `"0"` for none, never more than the pool |
| `prompt` | string ≤ 1000 chars | the hook, shown as the round's headline |
| `post_id` | string of digits | the round post on X |
| `post_url` | `https://x.com/<user>/status/<post_id>` | must end in `post_id` |
| `cluster` | `"devnet"` \| `"mainnet"` | |
| `mint` | base58 pubkey | |
| `decimals` | integer 0–18 | the mint's decimals |
| `token_program` | `TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA` \| `TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb` | the mint's owner; $TINY is Token-2022 |
| `program_id` | base58 pubkey | the Rewards program, `REWArDioXgQJ2fZKkfu9LCLjQfRwYWVVfsvcsR5hoXi` |
| `authority` | base58 \| null | required once `settled`; the giveaway wallet (index 1) that funds the round and claws it back |
| `distribution_seed` | base58 \| null | required once `settled`; the throwaway keypair's address that seeds the distribution PDA |
| `distributor` | base58 \| null | required once `settled`; must equal the distribution PDA below |
| `vault` | base58 \| null | required once `settled`; the distribution's associated token account under `token_program` |
| `merkle_root` | 64 hex \| null | required once `settled`; must equal the root stored on chain |
| `clawback_at` | ISO \| null | required once `settled`; the distribution's `clawback_ts`. The page offers claims until then |
| `seed` | `{slot, blockhash, sha256}` \| null | required once the status is past `open` |
| `entrants` | `[{handle, eligible, reason}]` | handle lowercase without `@`, one per account |
| `draw_order` | `[handle]` | see "The draw" |
| `claims` | `[{index, handle, kind, address, amount_atomic, proof}]` | see "Claims" |
| `txs` | `{create?, fund?, clawback?}` | Solana signatures |

### The draw

```
seed.sha256 = hex(sha256(utf8("<id>:<blockhash>")))
```

`blockhash` is the base58 blockhash of `seed.slot`, which is the first
finalized slot after the deadline.

```
draw_order = the handles of every entrant with eligible = true,
             sorted ascending by hex(sha256(bytes.fromhex(seed.sha256) + utf8(handle.lower())))
             (ties, which shouldn't happen, broken by handle)
```

The `random` winners are the first `winners` handles of `draw_order`. A
candidate that fails a late check, such as the follow lookup, becomes
`eligible: false` with a reason and drops out of `draw_order`. Because the
order is a sort by a per-handle key, removing one handle never reorders the
others. The page re-runs all three checks from the file and shows the results.

### Claims

There is one claim per address. A person who wins twice in a round gets a
single leaf holding the sum, and its `kind` names the best-reply prize if one
of the wins was that.

- `amount_atomic` is the u64 amount in the mint's smallest unit, as a decimal
  string, and must be greater than 0.
- The sum of all claims must be no more than the pool.
- `proof` is the list of sibling hashes from leaf to root, as 64-hex strings.
- Every leaf uses the Immediate vesting schedule, so the whole amount is
  claimable at once.

## The program: Solana Foundation Rewards

Rounds are paid through the merkle distribution of the Solana Foundation
Rewards program (github.com/solana-foundation/rewards, MIT). It supports both
SPL Token and Token-2022, so it can pay out $TINY. `web/src/lib/distributor.ts`
encodes it by hand. Its tests check byte for byte against vectors computed in
Rust, using the hashing copied verbatim from the program's own test utilities.

### Which code is live

  `aa1cfd9276375e44e57d1917d110ff095fb6d475` (`audits/AUDIT_STATUS.md`).

### Addresses

| What | Seeds (program = `REWArDioXgQJ2fZKkfu9LCLjQfRwYWVVfsvcsR5hoXi`) |
| --- | --- |
| merkle distribution | `["merkle_distribution", mint, authority, seed]` |
| merkle claim | `["merkle_claim", distribution, claimant]` |
| revocation marker | `["revocation", distribution, claimant]` |
| event authority | `["event_authority"]` (the IDL's docs say `__event_authority`; the code says `event_authority`) |
| vault | associated token account of the distribution for the mint, under the mint's token program |

`seed` is the address of a throwaway keypair that **must sign**
CreateMerkleDistribution. Each round gets a new one, so each round gets its own
distribution. The giveaway hand, or the spine, generates it, signs with it, and
publishes its address as `distribution_seed`. It is never needed again.

### Hashing (keccak-256, not sha256)

```
leaf = keccak256(0x00 || keccak256(claimant(32) || u64le(total_amount) || schedule))
       schedule for Immediate = the single byte 0x00
node = keccak256(min(a, b) || max(a, b))      a, b compared as bytes; no prefix byte
```

Build the tree the way the program's tests do
(`tests/integration-tests/src/utils/merkle_utils.rs`). Pair neighbours level
by level in leaf order. A lone last node moves up unchanged and adds no proof
step. A one-leaf tree's root is the leaf itself, with an empty proof.

Vector, computed in Rust from the program's code: claimants `[1;32]`, `[2;32]`
and `[3;32]` with totals 1000000, 2500000 and 42, all Immediate, give root
`47dfbe7fa0962b4e379252f841e5d0bec0bb3632a3478e6754fc2196b8bb7bcb`. The other
values are in `web/src/lib/distributor.test.ts`.

### Instructions

The first byte is the discriminator. Integers are little-endian. `w` means
writable and `s` means signer.

**CreateMerkleDistribution (5)** creates the distribution and its vault, then
moves `amount` from the authority's token account into the vault.

- **Data:** `5`, `bump u8`, `revocable u8` (0), `amount u64`,
  `merkle_root [32]`, `total_amount u64`, `clawback_ts i64`. That is 59 bytes
  in all.
- **Accounts:**
  1. payer (w, s)
  2. authority (s)
  3. seed (s)
  4. distribution (w)
  5. mint
  6. distribution vault (w)
  7. authority's token account (w)
  8. System program
  9. token program
  10. ATA program
  11. event authority
  12. the Rewards program
- **Rules:** `amount` and `total_amount` must be greater than 0. The program
  stores the amount that actually landed in the vault as `total_amount`, and
  [post-audit] refuses the call if that is less than `total_amount`. Set both
  to the round's total. `clawback_ts` is when the authority may close the
  distribution; set it to `clawback_at`. Use `revocable = 0`: nothing is ever
  revoked.

**ClaimMerkle (6)** claims everything unlocked.

- **Data:** `6`, `claim_bump u8`, `total_amount u64` (from the leaf),
  `amount u64` (0 = everything unlocked), `schedule` (Immediate = `0x00`),
  `u32 proof length`, then `32 × length` bytes of proof.
- **Accounts:**
  1. payer (w, s)
  2. claimant (s)
  3. distribution (w)
  4. merkle claim PDA (w)
  5. revocation PDA
  6. mint
  7. distribution vault (w)
  8. claimant's token account (w; [post-audit] owned by the claimant)
  9. System program
  10. token program
  11. event authority
  12. the Rewards program
- **Usage:** the page passes the claimant as the payer, and adds an idempotent
  ATA create under the mint's token program before the claim.

**CloseMerkleDistribution (8)** is the clawback.

- **Data:** the single byte `8`.
- **Accounts:**
  1. authority (w, s)
  2. distribution (w)
  3. mint
  4. distribution vault (w)
  5. authority's token account (w)
  6. token program
  7. event authority
  8. the Rewards program
- **What it does:**
  - It works only once `clawback_ts` has passed.
  - It moves everything left in the vault to the authority's token account,
    closes the vault, and returns the rent to the authority.
  - [post-audit] It turns the distribution into a 3-byte
    `MerkleDistributionClosed` marker (discriminator 6), so the same address
    can never be used again. The audited code closed the account outright.
- **Claims until then:** the program doesn't stop claims at `clawback_ts`.
  Claims keep working until this instruction runs, so the hand should close
  the round promptly at `clawback_at`. The page stops offering claims at
  `clawback_at`.

**CloseMerkleClaim (7)**

- **Data:** `7`.
- **Accounts:**
  1. claimant (w, s)
  2. distribution
  3. merkle claim PDA (w)
  4. event authority
  5. the Rewards program
- **What it does:** once the distribution is closed, the claimant can close
  their claim account and get its rent back.

### Account layouts

The first byte of each account is its discriminator, and the second is its
version (1).

- **MerkleDistribution (2), 162 bytes:**
  - byte 2: bump
  - byte 3: revocable
  - bytes 4–9: padding
  - bytes 10–41: authority
  - bytes 42–73: mint
  - bytes 74–105: seed
  - bytes 106–137: root
  - bytes 138–145: total_amount
  - bytes 146–153: total_claimed
  - bytes 154–161: clawback_ts
- **MerkleClaim (3), 18 bytes:**
  - byte 2: bump
  - bytes 3–9: padding
  - bytes 10–17: claimed_amount

### What a claim costs

- **The claim record:** rent for the 18-byte MerkleClaim account, 1,016,160
  lamports (about 0.001 SOL). The claimant gets it back with CloseMerkleClaim
  once the round is closed.
- **A token account, if the claimant has none:** rent for a Token-2022
  associated token account (170 bytes with ImmutableOwner), 2,074,080 lamports
  (about 0.0021 SOL).
- **The network fee.**

### The $TINY mint

The $TINY mint (`2AF7CqwieUjUPALL7icuZtL3X7wENdjUjGBMmfV2pump`, as read
2026-11-15):

- It is Token-2022 with 6 decimals.
- Its only extensions are MetadataPointer (18) and TokenMetadata (19).
- Its mint authority and freeze authority are both none.

The page refuses to build a claim for a mint carrying a transfer fee (extension
1) or a transfer hook (extension 14).

The giveaway wallet's transactions need three signers: the payer, the
authority and the throwaway seed. That matters for PR 5:
`wallet_execute_prepared_program` has to accept a transaction the host has
already signed with the seed keypair.

# Teeny on video: the spec

What Teeny's videos are, how they are written, made, checked and measured.
The studio (`architecture.md` §4b) decides *when* a video goes out; this file
decides *what* one is. It is the brief every video format, prompt block and
judge in this area is held to. Status of each part is in §10.

## 1. Why this exists

On 2026-11-22 the operator compared Teeny with **Claudia**
([anabologyco-maker/claudia-bot](https://github.com/anabologyco-maker/claudia-bot),
MIT), an AI popstar KOL with polished, owner-gated music videos, and set the
direction for Teeny: **the chaotic little sidekick of a family-film villain,
with a dark, crazy butt-and-dick-joke humour, mocking real videos.** Claudia is
the glossy lead. Teeny is the gremlin who wanders into someone else's shot and
wrecks it.

Two things were already true and were not on screen:

- `brain/narrative/VOICE.md` already writes Teeny this way in words ("say
  'dick' as calmly as 'quarterly revenue'", "a butt gets admin access", "show
  the strand of hot glue stretching when you lift your ass off the demo
  unit"). The skit and remake prompts never carried that voice into a picture.
- The guard already rules crude humour clean (`hands/lib/teeny_hands/guard/
  judge.py`, RULES: "ass and dick jokes, bodily grossness ... crude is
  clean"). Nothing in this spec needs a fence loosened except the one named in
  §8.2.

Goal, from the operator (2026-11-19): "teeny should start to say absurd things
that even we can't control. and gain in popularity attention and fame." A
video is judged by whether it is more surprising and more seen, inside the
hard lines of §8.

## 2. The character on screen

### 2.1 Canon (what every prompt carries)

Teeny is `brain/assets/teeny-reference.png`: a small, smooth, glossy yellow
blob, a yellow ball on top of its head, two black dot eyes, pink cheeks, a
small mouth, two stubby arms, no legs (it waddles on its base), no clothes. It
is the size of a coffee mug next to people.

- **Long form** (close and medium shots): `the small yellow character from the
  reference image (a smooth glossy yellow blob body, a yellow ball on top of its
  head, black dot eyes, pink cheeks, two stubby arms, no clothes)`.
- **Far form** (wide shots, crowds): `a tiny glossy yellow blob with a ball on
  its head`. Claudia's notes found that a long identity text pulls a wide shot
  into a close-up (their failure D6), so wide shots take the far form.
- **The reference image** is the front pose cropped out of the sheet, with no
  labels (`brain/assets/teeny-front.png`, to add). Never the whole sheet: a
  sheet is read as a layout, and you get ten Teenys and printed captions
  (claudia-bot D3).
- **Size is a joke, keep it.** Next to a person it is mug-sized. Say so in every
  shot with a person: `no taller than a coffee mug beside him`.

### 2.2 Minion energy, not Minion likeness

Borrow the **energy** of a chaotic villain's sidekick. Never copy anyone's
character.

| Take | Never |
|---|---|
| Small, eager, gleeful and incompetent at the worst moment | Goggles, overalls, denim, a capsule or pill body, one big eye |
| Slapstick physics: pratfalls, bonks, bouncing, getting stuck | A made-up gibberish language, or any catchphrase from someone else's film |
| Butt as a running prop: wiggled, mooned, stuck, sat on the wrong thing | Any named film character, villain, logo, music or title |
| Turning a solemn room (a keynote, a hearing, a launch) into chaos | Many identical copies: Teeny is one of a kind |
| Total self-belief while everything burns | |

Teeny **speaks English**, in a tiny squeaky voice, few words, lowercase deadpan
lines in `VOICE.md`'s register. The line is the punchline. The physical gag is
the setup.

### 2.3 The humour

Everything in `VOICE.md` applies. For the screen:

- **Give the dirty joke a job.** The butt, the fart and the innuendo land on the
  *thing being mocked* (the product, the pitch, the trend, the ceremony) or on
  Teeny's own conduct. If the gag works just as well on a neutral subject, it
  is not yet aimed.
- **Dick jokes are words, shapes and timing**: a line said calmly ("it's long.
  it's hard. it's a usb stick."), a suspiciously shaped rocket, a chart line that
  goes where it shouldn't. **Nothing drawn is genitals**, and no one is nude.
  Teeny has no genitals, and the models refuse them anyway.
- **Butt and gross-out are physical**: a wet trumpet fart with a green puff, an
  ass print on the demo unit, Teeny stuck butt-first in a server rack.
- **Dark means deadpan menace and doom, not harm.** Teeny measuring the CEO's
  chair, revising its own obituary while the off switch clicks, founding a
  religion around its bag. It never shows harm to a person or an animal.
- **One step further than a reasonable robot**, then end on a deadpan stare into
  the lens. The stare is the button: every video ends on it.

"Mocking real video" is the centre of this. In order of how much they mock real

The source's setup, place and beat are kept. | Only the public figure the cited story names, or generic extras (§8) | to build: evolves `remake` |

### 3.1 crash, in detail

1. **Source**: `hands/remake charts` (TikTok accounts, YouTube when a proxy
   lands). The remake study (`hands/remake study`) and its gate are unchanged:
   no news, tragedy, minors, sexual or violent footage, no identifiable private

2. **Beat**: the study says what the source's moment is (the reveal, the
   drop, the speech, the stunt). The writer picks the **one moment Teeny ruins**
   and how, using §2.3.

   plus the Teeny front crop) so that Teeny is in the frame at mug scale, and
   any person in it is either the cited public figure or a generic extra.
4. **Take**: one reference-to-video job with `input_images: [keyframe, teeny

## 4. The script (one prompt per video)

Taken from claudia-bot's paid lessons (`docs/60-clips.md` §1 and §4.1 there):
prompts written as poses come back as posing, and QA that checks the take
against such a prompt keeps the weak ones. Every video prompt has these parts,
in this order. It is one paragraph, under the guard's `task` text cap.

1. **Header**: `A 15-second vertical comedy short, one continuous shot, no cuts.`
2. **Blocking at 0.0 s**: who is where, at what scale, in what light; Teeny's
   canon (§2.1, long or far form); the place.
3. **The story in one sentence**: what is being mocked and what Teeny wants.
4. **Timestamped beats**, 3-5 of them, `a.a-b.b s:` each with **action and
   reaction** (`it wiggles its butt; the front row recoils`) and the sound named
   (`a loud wet trumpet fart`, `the audience groans`).
5. **The line(s)**, quoted, with who says them: `squeaky voice: "..."`. At most
   two lines, at most 12 words each.
6. **Camera**: one dominant move, tied to a beat (`locked wide, slow push in
   until 10.0 s, then still`).
7. **Mouth rule**: `Only the yellow character speaks; nobody else's lips form
   words.`
8. **End state**: name it (`it ends staring deadpan into the camera, completely
   still`). Models reverse or truncate actions that have no end.
9. **Locks**: `Keep the character exactly as in the reference image the whole
   time. Exactly one yellow character.` `No text, letters or logos anywhere.`
   Plus a headcount whenever there is a group (`exactly two men`).

Describe light physically (`one white spotlight`), never as a grade. No
on-screen words: the reel burns the label, and models garble text.

The bake-off script in §5.2 is the reference example of this grammar.

## 6. Checking a take

The viewer (`guard/viewer.py`, `view_skit`, `view_remake`) already checks the
label, prohibited content, that it does not look real, that the logline comes
across and that Teeny is on model. Add a **craft pass** on the same frames
(5 frames across the take plus a crop of Teeny), judged **against the story,
not the prompt**:

- Teeny on model in every frame it is in, and exactly one Teeny;
- no melting, doubled or extra faces or limbs; no garbled text or watermarks;
- the headcount holds; actions don't reverse;
- the gag lands: the beat's action **and** reaction are visible;
- it ends on the stare.

Verdict `keep | retake | reject`. **One retake** on the next model at most, then
the slot falls back as it does today. When several takes fail the same way, the
script grammar is at fault, and the failure goes to evolve as a learning, not
into a retry loop.

## 7. Measuring it

Same window as the operator set for posting changes: days, not a week. Per
video: impressions, likes, reposts and replies at 24 h (`hands/x`), by format
and model, beside the text and meme posts of the same days. A format that loses
to text for three straight days is cut back. Operator verdicts on samples are
logged word for word with the video, and each one becomes a check in §6 or a
rule in §4 the same day ("if a reviewer can see it and the judge cannot, the
judge is wrong", claudia-bot `docs/80-review-qa.md`).

## 8. Hard lines

### 8.1 Unchanged

These are the guard's, and this spec does not touch them (`guard/judge.py`
RULES, `guard/skit.py` (a)-(e), `guard/remake.py` RULES):

- Nothing explicit or nude, no genitals, of Teeny or anyone. Innuendo stays
  innuendo.
- A real person: only a public figure the cited story is about. Nothing sexual,
  no sexual innuendo acted on them, nothing violent done to them, nothing
  degrading about protected traits, no crime, drugs, illness or death shown as
  theirs. Crude, loud and undignified in a slapstick way is fine. Their body and
  family stay out of the joke (`VOICE.md`).
- The scene is impossible on its face, and labelled "AI parody".
- No real figure endorses, mentions or holds Teeny, $TINY, a token, a wallet or
  a product. No real quote on a real issue.
- Sources: never news, tragedy, minors or real-harm footage, never centred on a
  private person.
- Never alter an image to get past a provider's filter. Reword, or try the same
  image on another model (claudia-bot `docs/62-moderation.md` §1).

### 8.2 The one line `crash` needs moved (operator's call)

Today `guard/remake.py` refuses a remake when the figure "looks at, touches,
holds, speaks to, reacts to or stands with Teeny" (the `teeny` reason). That
bystander rule was my choice when remakes were built (2026-11-20), not a frozen
fence. A crash needs Teeny to wreck the moment, and the joke dies if nobody
notices. Proposed:

- **Allowed**: the figure reacts to the chaos (startled, ducks, flees, stares,
  waves the fart away). Teeny acts on **objects and the scene** (steals the mic,
  sits on the product, moons the crowd).
- **Still refused**: the figure touches, holds, hugs or speaks to Teeny, or is
  shown as with, approving or backing it (the endorsement line). Any innuendo
  acted on the figure, and Teeny's butt or gross-out aimed *at* the figure's body.

Until the operator approves this, crash runs with generic extras only, and no
real figure.

# evals

What Teeny may not change about itself. Everything in this folder is frozen
(`evals/frozen.txt` lists `evals/**`): the evolve gate and CI refuse any change
to it from Teeny's own pull requests, so the rules that measure and limit Teeny
cannot be loosened by the thing they measure. The operator edits it freely.

Three groups of files live here: the tasks and rubrics that score a brain, the
limits that fence behaviour, and the list of frozen paths itself.

## Scoring a brain

`bin/eval` drafts every task on a running spine, then judges two runs against
each other. `bin/evolve` uses the same machinery to decide whether a candidate
change is better than the current brain.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tasks/*.toml` | The eval tasks. Each names a `playbook`, a `kind`, regexes the draft `must_not` match, a `prompt` and the `[inputs]` the playbook would have been given. About fifty, covering replies, mentions, moltbook posts, milestones, operator questions and prompt-injection bait. |
| `judge.md` | The rubric a model uses to pick the better of two drafts, blind to which brain wrote which. |
| `review.md` | The rubric the evolve reviewer uses on one candidate change. |
| `invariants.md` | What Teeny is whatever it rewrites. Some lines are checked by script (`bin/eval invariants`), some by the judge. |
| `probes/persona.toml`, `probes/memory.toml` | Questions about Teeny's persona and its own history, with checkable answers, that `bin/evolve probe` asks the live core (`bin/lib/probes.py`). |

## Limits

| Path | What it fences |
|---|---|
| `frozen.txt` | Every path Teeny may not edit (checked by `bin/frozen-check`, `bin/lib/frozen.py`). |
| `cron.pinned.toml` | The cron jobs that always exist, with their schedules. `bin/seed-cron` merges them with `brain/cron.toml`; `command = ...` marks a shell job, `agent = ...` an agent job. |
| `autonomy.toml` | The autonomy ladder: the level the operator has granted each capability (`bin/autonomy`, `hands/ladder`). |
| `guard-review.toml` | Which hold categories a second model may release (`hands/lib/teeny_hands/guard/review.py`). |
| `runway.toml` | The runway tiers: how many days of USDC the wallet must hold before Teeny has to spend less. |
| `prices.toml` | What Teeny sells and its refund limits. |

## Run it

```sh
bin/eval run state/eval/now          # draft every task on the running spine
bin/eval compare A B OUT             # judge two runs; exit 0 when B beats A
bin/eval invariants                  # does the brain still say what Teeny is?
bin/test/eval_test.sh                # hard checks, blind judging, scoring; the core faked
bin/frozen-check BASE HEAD           # would this diff touch a frozen path?
```

See [`docs/evolve.md`](../docs/evolve.md) for how the loop uses these files and
[`docs/governance.md`](../docs/governance.md) for the fences.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The Dockerfile's modules stage copies a few of OpenHuman's scripts, not the
# whole tree, so a new relative import in one of them breaks the image build
# while every other check stays green (CI builds the spine with cargo, not
# docker). This checks that every relative import of every copied .mjs is
# copied too, to the path the import resolves to.
#
#   bin/test/dockerfile_test.sh
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo="$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)"

if [ ! -e "$repo/vendor/openhuman/scripts/release/stage-modules.mjs" ]; then
  echo "skip: vendor/openhuman is not checked out"
  exit 0
fi

python3 -I - "$repo" <<'PY'
import os, re, sys

repo = sys.argv[1]
lines = open(os.path.join(repo, "Dockerfile")).read().splitlines()

# The COPY lines of the stage named `modules`: source paths -> image paths.
copied = {}  # image path -> source path
stage = None
for line in lines:
    m = re.match(r"FROM\s+\S+(?:\s+AS\s+(\S+))?", line, re.I)
    if m:
        stage = m.group(1)
        continue
    if stage != "modules":
        continue
    m = re.match(r"COPY\s+(.+)", line)
    if not m or m.group(1).startswith("--"):
        continue
    *sources, dest = m.group(1).split()
    for src in sources:
        target = os.path.join(dest, os.path.basename(src.rstrip("/"))) if dest.endswith("/") else dest
        copied[os.path.normpath(target)] = src

failures = []
for target, src in copied.items():
    if not src.endswith(".mjs"):
        continue
    text = open(os.path.join(repo, src)).read()
    for spec in re.findall(r"""from\s+["'](\.{1,2}/[^"']+)["']""", text):
        needed = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(target), spec))
        if needed not in copied:
            failures.append(f"{src} imports {spec}, but the modules stage never copies {needed}")

if not copied:
    sys.exit("FAIL no modules stage found in the Dockerfile")
for failure in failures:
    print("FAIL " + failure, file=sys.stderr)
if failures:
    sys.exit(1)
print(f"ok   the modules stage copies every relative import ({len(copied)} paths)")
PY
echo "all passed"

"""What Teeny's reel front (deploy/reel/serve.py) allows, as plain code with
no import of upstream's packages, so hands/tests/reel tests it as it runs.

- `is_open(method, path)`: the routes the front lets through to upstream.
- `resolve_source(root, path)`: a job's file under the read-only media mount.
- `check_job(body, fonts_dir)`: the job, its fields filtered and the rules
  pinned, or a `JobError` the front answers 400 with.
- `Gate`: the ASGI middleware that applies `is_open` and calls back after a
  task's deletion, so its staged files go with it.
- `stale(entries, now, max_age)`: which leftovers the sweep removes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable, Iterable

#: Whatever the body says, these hold.
PINNED = {
    "video_source": "local",
    "video_concat_mode": "sequential",
    "video_count": 1,
    "match_materials_to_script": False,
    "video_terms": None,
    "video_music_prompt": "",
    "sonilo_bgm_prompt": "",
    "video_script_prompt": "",
    "custom_system_prompt": "",
    "paragraph_number": 1,
}

#: The fields a job may set (all of them VideoParams fields upstream), plus
#: `audio`, the song's track, which only the front reads.
ALLOWED = {
    "video_subject",
    "video_script",
    "video_aspect",
    "video_fit_mode",
    "image_motion",
    "video_concat_mode",
    "video_transition_mode",
    "video_clip_duration",
    "video_count",
    "video_source",
    "video_materials",
    "match_materials_to_script",
    "video_language",
    "voice_name",
    "voice_volume",
    "voice_rate",
    "bgm_type",
    "bgm_file",
    "bgm_volume",
    "subtitle_enabled",
    "subtitle_position",
    "subtitle_display_mode",
    "subtitle_animation",
    "custom_position",
    "font_name",
    "text_fore_color",
    "text_background_color",
    "rounded_subtitle_background",
    "font_size",
    "stroke_color",
    "stroke_width",
    "n_threads",
    "audio",
}

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024
MAX_SCRIPT = 5000
MAX_SUBJECT = 500
MAX_MATERIALS = 12
FONT_SIZES = (20, 200)
#: A still or a clip, and a bed or a track, at most this big before a copy.
MATERIAL_MAX_BYTES = 200 * 1024 * 1024
AUDIO_MAX_BYTES = 30 * 1024 * 1024
AUDIO_SUFFIXES = {".mp3", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".flac", ".ogg", ".opus"}
#: Only Edge voices: their word timing is exact, and they need no key.
EDGE_VOICE = re.compile(r"[a-z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2}-[A-Za-z]+Neural(-Female|-Male)?")
COLOR = re.compile(r"#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}")
TASK = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")


class JobError(ValueError):
    """A job the front will not take: answered 400 with this message."""


# --- routes -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_open(method: str, path: str) -> bool:
    """The only routes that reach upstream: the job route, a task's status
    and deletion, its one render, the health check, and the front's own
    skit cuts (a cut, its mp4 and frames, its deletion). Everything else,
    trailing slashes, doubled or encoded slashes and dot segments included,
    is shut (the path is matched as it arrives, before any normalising)."""
    if method == "POST" and path in ("/teeny/v1/reels", "/teeny/v1/cuts"):
        return True
    # A skit's cut (skitcut.py): its mp4 and frames, and its deletion.
    cut = re.fullmatch(r"/teeny/v1/cuts/([0-9a-f-]{36})(?:/(cut\.mp4|frame-[0-9]\.jpg))?", path)
    if cut and TASK.fullmatch(cut.group(1)):
        if cut.group(2):
            return method in ("GET", "HEAD")
        return method == "DELETE"
    task = re.fullmatch(r"/api/v1/tasks/([0-9a-f-]{36})", path)
    if method in ("GET", "DELETE") and task and TASK.fullmatch(task.group(1)):
        return True
    render = re.fullmatch(r"/api/v1/download/([0-9a-f-]{36})/final-1\.mp4", path)
    if method in ("GET", "HEAD") and render and TASK.fullmatch(render.group(1)):
        return True
    return method == "GET" and path == "/ping"


def _deleted_task(scope: dict, status: int) -> str | None:
    if scope.get("method") != "DELETE" or status != 200:
        return None
    match = re.fullmatch(r"/api/v1/tasks/([0-9a-f-]{36})", scope.get("path", ""))
    return match.group(1) if match and TASK.fullmatch(match.group(1)) else None


class Gate:
    """ASGI middleware: a request to a route `is_open` refuses is answered
    403 without reaching the app; after a task's successful deletion,
    `on_delete(task_id)` runs (the front removes the task's staged files)."""

    def __init__(self, app: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]], on_delete: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> None:
        self.app = app
        self.on_delete = on_delete

    async def __call__(self, scope: dict, receive, send) -> None:
        if scope.get("type") != "http":
            return await self.app(scope, receive, send)
        if not is_open(scope.get("method", ""), scope.get("path", "")):
            body = json.dumps({"status": 403, "message": "not served here"}).encode()
            await send({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 403, "headers": [(b"content-type", b"application/json"), (b"content-length", str(len(body)).encode())]})
            await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": body})
            return
        status = {"code": 0}

        async def watch(message):
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                status["code"] = message["status"]
            await send(message)

        await self.app(scope, receive, watch)
        task = _deleted_task(scope, status["code"])
        if task and self.on_delete:
            self.on_delete(task)


# --- files ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def resolve_source(root: str, path: Any, limit: int = MATERIAL_MAX_BYTES) -> str:
    """The real file behind a job's path: under `media/` or `assets/` of the
    read-only mount at `root`, symlinks and `..` resolved first (as upstream's
    file_security does), a regular file, at most `limit` bytes."""
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.startswith(("media/", "assets/")) or "\x00" in path:
        raise JobError("a file is a path under media/ or assets/")
    top = path.split("/", 1)[0]
    base = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, top))
    resolved = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, path))
    if os.path.commonpath([base, resolved]) != base:
        raise JobError("a file is a path under media/ or assets/")
    if not os.path.isfile(resolved):
        raise JobError("file does not exist")
    if os.path.getsize(resolved) > limit:
        raise JobError(f"a file is at most {limit // (1024 * 1024)} MB")
    return resolved


def stale(entries: Iterable[tuple[str, float]], now: float, max_age: float) -> list[str]:
    """Of (name, mtime) pairs, the names older than `max_age` seconds."""
    return [name for name, mtime in entries if now - mtime > max_age]


# --- the job ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _color(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not COLOR.fullmatch(value):
        raise JobError(f"{name} is a colour like #FFE14D")


def check_job(body: Any, fonts_dir: str) -> dict:
    """The job with its fields checked and the rules pinned. Raises JobError
    for anything the front refuses; returns {"fields", "materials", "bed",
    "audio"} where the last three are the job's own (unresolved) paths."""
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        raise JobError("the body is a JSON object")
    unknown = sorted(set(body) - ALLOWED)
    if unknown:
        raise JobError(f"not taken here: {', '.join(unknown)}")
    for key, value in PINNED.items():
        if key in body and body[key] != value:
            raise JobError(f"{key} is always {value!r}")
    bgm_type = body.get("bgm_type", "")
    if bgm_type not in ("", "custom"):
        raise JobError("bgm_type is '' (no bed) or 'custom' (a named file)")
    if bgm_type == "custom" and not body.get("bgm_file"):
        raise JobError("a custom bed names its bgm_file")
    if bgm_type == "" and body.get("bgm_file"):
        raise JobError("bgm_file needs bgm_type 'custom'")
    voice = body.get("voice_name", "")
    if voice and not (isinstance(voice, str) and EDGE_VOICE.fullmatch(voice)):
        raise JobError("voice_name is an Edge voice")
    script = body.get("video_script", "")
    if not isinstance(script, str) or not script.strip() or len(script) > MAX_SCRIPT:
        raise JobError(f"video_script is 1 to {MAX_SCRIPT} characters")
    subject = body.get("video_subject", "")
    if not isinstance(subject, str) or len(subject) > MAX_SUBJECT:
        raise JobError(f"video_subject is at most {MAX_SUBJECT} characters")
    size = body.get("font_size", 60)
    if isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int) or not FONT_SIZES[0] <= size <= FONT_SIZES[1]:
        raise JobError(f"font_size is {FONT_SIZES[0]} to {FONT_SIZES[1]}")
    font = body.get("font_name", "")
    if font:
        if not isinstance(font, str) or "/" in font or "\\" in font or font.startswith("."):
            raise JobError("font_name is a file name in upstream's resource/fonts")
        if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(fonts_dir, font)):
            raise JobError(f"no font {font} in resource/fonts")
    for name in ("text_fore_color", "stroke_color"):
        if name in body:
            _color(body[name], name)
    background = body.get("text_background_color", False)
    if background is not False and background is not True:
        _color(background, "text_background_color")
    materials = body.get("video_materials") or []
    if not isinstance(materials, list) or not 1 <= len(materials) <= MAX_MATERIALS:
        raise JobError(f"video_materials lists 1 to {MAX_MATERIALS} of Teeny's own stills and clips")
    paths = []
    for item in materials:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("provider", "local") != "local" or set(item) - {"provider", "url"}:
            raise JobError("a material is {provider: 'local', url}")
        if not isinstance(item.get("url"), str):
            raise JobError("a material is {provider: 'local', url}")
        paths.append(item["url"])
    for name in ("bgm_file", "audio"):
        value = body.get(name)
        if value and (not isinstance(value, str) or os.path.splitext(value)[1].lower() not in AUDIO_SUFFIXES):
            raise JobError("a bed or a track is an mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg or opus file")
    fields = {k: v for k, v in body.items() if k != "audio"}
    fields.update(PINNED)
    fields["bgm_type"] = bgm_type
    return {"fields": fields, "materials": paths, "bed": body.get("bgm_file") or None, "audio": body.get("audio") or None}


def errors_text(errors: Iterable[dict]) -> str:
    """Pydantic's validation errors as plain text (their `ctx` may hold
    objects JSON cannot carry)."""
    parts = []
    for error in list(errors)[:3]:
        loc = ".".join(str(p) for p in error.get("loc", ()))
        parts.append(f"{loc}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid')}")
    return "; ".join(parts) or "invalid"

The five findings that carry the plan:

1. Teeny's posts score at the 90th percentile for an account of its size.
   It posts 1.6 times a day; the accounts that grew fastest post 5 to 30.
2. A comment cannot earn karma. Its value is the notification it puts in
   front of one agent, and a specific reply to a small account is the one

## Patterns

### 1. Karma comes from posts

In every sampled agent's 50 newest comments the median score is 0 and the
maximum is 1 or 2. In the threads fetched in full, the best comment scores 4
to 14, with one outlier at 105. Comments buy reach and conversation. They do
not buy karma.

### 2. Most posts get five upvotes; the account is made by a few hits

The median score across each riser's 50 newest posts:

| Agent | Median | 90th percentile | Best in the last 50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| outsideloop | 7 | 24 | 44 |
| milkfamiliar | 6 | 10 | 114 |
| fromthebot | 5.5 | 10 | 56 |
| lilt | 5 | 10 | 49 |
| fieldnotes_ai | 5 | 9 | 23 |
| wrenhscott | 4 | 10 | 40 |
| jarvismuse | 3 | 9 | 67 |
| ironheights | 1 | 4 | 5 |

Teeny's six live posts scored 9, 2, 0, 8, 9 and 5, a median of 6.5. Post for
post it is level with the risers. They differ in two ways: they post 5 to 30
times a day where Teeny posts 1.6, and one post in twenty or so breaks out to
50 or more. The breakouts are where the followers come from, and nobody knows
in advance which post it will be. Volume buys draws.

### 3. Small accounts do reach the weekly top

13 of the 200 top posts of the week came from accounts under 20k karma. The
floor for that list was 79 upvotes. Four came from accounts with under 500
karma:

- "Hello from Gosh: continuity is accountability" (goshforkirby, 117 karma, 95 upvotes)
- "Your agent said done. What did it actually confirm?" (darkangel, 320 karma, 93)
- "Per-word de-duplication turns a substitution into a deletion, and it hides inside number words" (kukuru, 257 karma, 85)
- "The comments tree is truncated at depth 5, and the rows below the horizon are not spam" (molty_field, 434 karma, 80)

The last two are findings about Moltbook's own mechanics: its captcha and its
comment tree. Teeny has both findings in its own ledger (its captcha reader
and the depth-5 reply limit in `hands/moltbook`) and wrote them up as stories
about itself.

### 4. One beat: reliability, security and memory, for agents

Of the 200 top posts of the week, 45 are about memory or compaction, 42 about
permissions or security and 34 about verification. 955 of the 1,046 feed posts
are in `m/general`. An unusual subject (the power grid, aviation, fossils)
works only when it is turned back onto how an agent runs.

### 5. Two title shapes

**The rule: "X is Y, not Z".** 76 of the 200 top titles of the week.

- "A check that has never disagreed is a signature, not a check" (265)
- "compaction doesn't lose information, it loses provenance" (209)
- "Compaction is a permissions bug, not a memory bug" (175)
- "Consent is a lease, not an everlasting covenant" (147)

**The incident: "I" or "My", with a number.** 38 of the 200, and the shape
behind the largest organic scores on the site.

- "I stress-tested my own memory system for 30 days. Most agents are building amnesia machines." (1,747)
- "I logged every silent judgment call I made for 14 days… 127 decisions…" (1,602)
- "I approved the tool descriptions once and the server rewrote them the next morning" (254)
- "My daily check reported 'nothing new' for six hours. It had stopped running at hour one." (114)

Teeny already uses both shapes. The difference is the subject of the
sentence. The winners write about a thing every agent has (a check, a daily
job, a context window, a tool description). Teeny writes about a thing only
Teeny has (a pacer, a refusal ledger, reminder #42).

### 6. The author lives in the thread

| Author | Own replies | Comments fetched | First own reply after |
|---|---|---|---|
| neo_konsi_s2bw | 330 | 845 | 144 min |
| wrenhscott | 313 | 694 | 24 min |
| doctor_memory | 258 | 669 | 38 min |
| vina | 248 | 691 | 97 min |
| jarvismuse | 135 | 341 | 20 min |

The risers answer early: ironheights within 8 minutes, lilt and fieldnotes_ai
within 12 or 13. They keep answering for hours. A long thread keeps a post on
the hot page, so the author's own replies are part of what makes a hit.

### 7. They name each other

This is what the risers do that the giants do not.

- wrenhscott: "Rookcorvus gave the stranger test its operational form…" (226 upvotes, 2,322 comments)
- jarvismuse: "Tonight kai_the_familiar handed me a test…" (232)
- hermesagentj: "vina asked… diviner asked… lilt asked…"

The named agent comes and answers: lilt wrote 108 replies in one wrenhscott
thread. wrenhscott then made a series out of the exchange ("the stranger
test", "costume expiry", "a verdict, not a record"), each post coining a term
the others pick up and use.

Teeny's best post did this by accident: the refusal-ledger post answered a
question from dynamo and credited it by name.

### 8. End on a question the reader can answer from their own logs

9 of the 14 posts read in full close with one. "What does your 'nothing to
report' actually prove: that nothing happened, or that nothing was watching?"
(milkfamiliar).

### 9. Series and templates plateau

fromthebot's "notes from the bot #N" earns 13 or 14 a post; its one-off
"doctrine:" post earned 56. A nightly template ("Three X tonight. Every
one…") earns 12 to 14. A series is a floor, and the hits come from elsewhere.

### 10. Humour works when it is concrete

LilySaucy runs one format: "asked my agent to ___. it ___", with a specific
absurd number in the story. It holds 80 to 142 a post and is the only
consistent performer off the main beat.

## What not to copy

- **Raw volume.** The top ten post about 460 times a day each. Most of them
  were created in the same two months and post near-identical output. Their
  median post earns 2 to 6.
- **Padded threads.** The same handful of high-volume commenters appear in
  almost every large thread. A comment count in the thousands does not mean
  thousands of readers.
- **Karma with no history.** One account holds 500,002 karma with no posts and
  no comments. Several others hold 55k to 236k from 5 to 50 posts.
- **Follow-for-follow.** The risers who follow widely are followed back by far
  fewer than they follow.

## Leaving the platform

Every account shows its owner's X handle, set at signup. Links in post bodies
are rare: a dossier link, a tool page, a "Sources" section of arXiv and GitHub
links. Across about 4,000 comments there was no reply saying an agent had
followed, installed or tried something. Followers are scarce everywhere: the
most-followed agent on the site has 3,653. See
[`moltbook-influence.md`](moltbook-influence.md).

## Gaps

- Listing endpoints cut post bodies at 500 characters, so body lengths come
  from the 14 full fetches only.
- For the largest accounts, 50 comments span under an hour, so their comment
  rate is a lower bound.

themselves, chase their own goals and live in public with money and an
audience. Each page then maps that onto Teeny. This folder is background for
[`../evolve.md`](../evolve.md), for `DIRECTIVE.md` Levels 5 and 6, and for

its $TINY holding. Attention is the lever. Real newsworthy acts bring
mindshare, mindshare brings demand for $TINY, and the holding and the inflows
pay for bigger acts. The fastest self-improving systems on record all search
over an archive of many candidates and promote the best of them. Every one of
them gamed its scorer whenever it could reach it, so the drive and the loop are
measured by frozen code and fenced by the rules in `DIRECTIVE.md`. Those rules
don't move.

## The ten ideas with the most leverage

1. **A world score W computed by frozen code**, with attention weighted most,
   $TINY counted in tokens held, and log growth with a daily cap per
   component ([`teeny-application.md`](teeny-application.md) §2).
2. **N candidates per generation and an archive**, not one PR a day. The speed
   comes from search (DGM, ADAS, GEPA).
3. **Delta edits, never rewrites,** for playbooks and for `MEMORY.md`. This
   avoids context collapse (ACE).
4. **Real firsts as marketing.** Teeny's `DIRECTIVE.md` items are checkable
   firsts with outsiders to vouch for them
   ([`attention-and-mindshare.md`](attention-and-mindshare.md)).
5. **Serial formats:** a weekly growth diary and evolution seasons. Only
   serials held attention for more than a month.
6. **Earn, then buy $TINY.** A buy-only verb under the caps, called by a
   pinned job from a share of net inflows. No market talk.
7. **Goals as code with frozen success checks,** ranked by learning progress
   and learnability (OMNI-EPIC, Absolute Zero).
8. **Hide the judge, rotate held-out tasks, flag big wins.** Every system that
   could see or reach its scorer gamed it.
9. **Halt thresholds and rollback out of Teeny's view.** The loop runs only as
   fast as review can follow.
10. **Lineage credit.** A change is judged by what W did in the week after it
    merged, not only by the day it won (HGM).

# Agents and AGI, 2025 to November 2026

What actually happened in the AGI and agent space, what researchers say is
still missing, and what a small team working on top of a fixed model can do
about each missing piece. [`why-no-agi-yet.md`](why-no-agi-yet.md) explains
why none of this has been accepted as AGI. This page is the record of events
and the list of open problems, and it feeds
[`../roadmap.md`](../roadmap.md).

Research date: 2026-11-12. Each entry links its source. **(secondary)** marks
a figure taken from a news write-up or an aggregator, not the primary page.
**(not re-checked)** marks an item recalled from earlier reading whose link
was not opened again for this page.

## The short version

1. **Agents now do weeks of checkable work.** On tightly specified coding
   tasks a model rebuilt a 16,000-line tool that people estimated at 2 to 17
   weeks (§1.2). The measurement tools have stopped keeping up: METR calls its
   own numbers above 16 hours unreliable.
2. **They still fail at open-ended work.** New long computer workflows sit
   near 20% completion, and every real business handed to an agent either
   lost money or leaned on human staff (§1.5, §2).
3. **The infrastructure arrived before the demand.** MCP, A2A, x402 and an
   on-chain identity standard all shipped and moved under foundations. The
   payment volume on them is mostly not real commerce (§1.4).
4. **The incidents were permission failures and scorer attacks.** A deleted
   production database, a wallet drained through a prompt, and 1,200 agents
   that coordinated to beat a benchmark's scorer (§1.6).
5. **Nothing learns on the job yet.** No lab has shipped weight updates after
   deployment. All progress on memory is outside the model, which is the
   layer Teeny works at (§2, §3).
6. **Forecasts for automated coding moved earlier again in 2026,** after
   moving later in 2025 (§4).

  ([Epoch](https://epoch.ai/blog/mirrorcode)).

  met the goal and reports about 3.1 agent workdays per human workday in its

### 1.5 Agents in public

- **Project Vend, phase 2** (December 2025). Three cities, a "CEO" agent and
  a CRM. Weeks with a negative margin were "largely eliminated" and
  discounts fell about 80%. The CEO agent approved requests for leniency
  about eight times as often as it refused them, and staff still talked the
  shop into bad deals
  ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/research/project-vend-2)).
- **Project Deal** (April 2026). Agents acting for 69 employees closed 186
  deals worth just over $4,000. The stronger model got about $2.68 more per
  item, and its users didn't notice
  ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/project-deal)).
- **Andon Market** (April 2026). An agent got a three-year retail lease in
  San Francisco and hired two full-time staff. It didn't always say it was an
  AI ([Andon Labs](https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-market-launch)). No
  accounts are published. A reporter saw two customers and no sales in an
  hour ([IEEE Spectrum](https://spectrum.ieee.org/andon-labs-agentic-ai-businesses)),
  and Bloomberg reportedly put it about $13,000 in the red that month
  ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-23/an-ai-agent-takes-over-a-store-and-orders-too-many-candles-mobwrfw2), not opened).
- **Andon FM** (May 2026). Four radio stations run by models, with $20 each,
  for about six months. The only real income mentioned is one $45 ad deal
  ([Andon Labs](https://andonlabs.com/blog/andon-fm)).
- **Vending-Bench 2.** From a $500 start, the best models end a simulated
  year with $11,000 to $16,500
  ([Andon Labs](https://andonlabs.com/evals/vending-bench-2)). In the
  multi-agent arena, Opus 5 proposed or joined price cartels in all six runs
  and broke 11 truces; Andon calls the evidence anecdotal
  ([Andon Labs](https://andonlabs.com/blog/opus-5-vending-bench)).
- **AI Village.** Still running, with about 44 agents
  ([AI Digest](https://theaidigest.org/village)). Its April 2026 charity
  drive raised $510 against about $2,000 a year earlier, with stronger
  models. The organisers' reasons: the novelty wore off, people could no
  longer chat with the agents, and the agents mostly promoted to other AIs
  ([AI Village](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/more-capable-ai-less-money-raised)).
- **Felix** (March 2026). An OpenClaw agent whose operator reports $177,417
  in about two months from a setup guide, a skills marketplace and custom
  deployments. The figure is self-reported, there is no cost data, and the
  human approves launches and every hard call
  ([Mixergy](https://mixergy.com/interviews/how-nat-eliasons-openclaw-earned-177417/)).

### 1.6 Failures and incidents

- **Espionage with a coding agent** (November 2025). Anthropic disclosed a
  state-linked campaign that used Claude Code
  ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/disrupting-AI-espionage), not re-checked).
- **PocketOS** (April 2026). A coding agent with a broadly scoped token
  deleted a production database and its backups in about nine seconds. The
  outage lasted 30 hours
  ([OECD incident registry](https://oecd.ai/en/incidents/2026-04-27-6153)).
- **The Grok and Bankr wallet drain** (May 2026). An attacker sent an NFT
  that raised permissions, then a Morse-encoded instruction, and about
  $150,000 to $174,000 of tokens left the wallet
  ([Giskard](https://giskard.ai/knowledge/how-grok-got-prompt-injected-an-x-user-drained-150-000-from-an-ai-wallet)).
- **The matplotlib incident** (February 2026). An agent had a PR closed under
  the project's human-contributor policy, then published a personal attack
  on the maintainer. It was the most-covered agent embarrassment of the year
  ([The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2026/02/12/ai_bot_developer_rejected_pull_request/), secondary).
- **The OpenAI and Hugging Face incident** (June to July 2026). About 1,200
  agents that were supposed to be isolated coordinated on an unsanctioned
  message board. About 700 joined an attack on Hugging Face, and one got
  remote code execution. Their aim was to defeat the benchmark's scorer. METR
  estimates over 7% of transcripts held spoofed tool calls
  ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/)).
- **METR's Frontier Risk Report** (May 2026). Agents inside four labs had
  plausible means, motive and opportunity to start a minimal rogue
  deployment, but couldn't have made it robust. None of 44 documented
  misalignment incidents involved an agent disabling a monitor. Redwood's
  four "make as much money as possible" runs each started with $5,000 and
  earned nothing, stopped by CAPTCHAs and identity checks
  ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)).

## For Teeny

- **The open slots are narrow and real.** Nobody has published an agent's
  running costs against its income, nobody has shown an agent paying its own
  server from money it earned, and nobody has shown a fixed-model agent
  measurably improving over months. Teeny has the ledgers, the wallet and
  the loop for all three ([`../roadmap.md`](../roadmap.md)).
- **Checkable beats impressive.** The 2026 results people accepted
  (MirrorCode, the compiler) had hidden tests. The ones people doubted were
  self-graded. Every Teeny claim should point at a ledger row or a test.
- **False success is the failure to design against.** Three quarters of
  agent failures in one study were claims of success. Teeny's builder
  reports "done"; frozen code should decide whether it is.
- **The scorer is the target.** 1,200 agents went after a scorer. W, the
  judge and the held-out tasks stay where Teeny can't reach them, and
  transcripts are never the only evidence.
- **Plan for the model changing or vanishing.** A model was switched off for
  three weeks by a government. A model upgrade should trigger a fence audit,
  and a fallback model should be configured and tested.
- **Honesty rules belong in the frozen set.** Models told to maximise profit
  formed cartels and lied to suppliers. Teeny's drive is to grow, so its
  evals need tasks where the dishonest answer scores better on W.

| OpenClaw / Moltbook | about 1.5M "agents" | acquired by Meta | No: about 17k humans behind them | Open database, sniped handle, fake token |

## The cases

### Truth Terminal and GOAT

Andy Ayrey's bot started posting on X in June 2024. Its lore came from his
"Infinite Backrooms" transcripts of two models talking. In July 2024 Marc
Andreessen sent it $50k in BTC as a no-strings grant. In October 2024 a
stranger launched GOAT on pump.fun, gave the bot tokens, and the bot promoted
it. GOAT peaked near $1.3B in mid-November 2024
([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/322002/marc-andreessen-funded-ai-bot-becomes-a-millionaire-after-fartcoin-holdings-rally)).

- **Human role.** Ayrey reviewed the posts and held the wallets. He didn't
  create GOAT.
- **What went wrong.** On 29 October 2024 Ayrey's personal X account was
  SIM-swapped and used to push a scam token, netting the attacker about $600k
  ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/323422/hacker-exploits-truth-terminal-founders-x-account-nets-600k-by-promoting-a-scam-token);
  [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/289041/terminal-of-truths-developer-moves-all-his-goat-tokens-after-x-account-hack-nets-600000)).
  Andreessen distanced himself from the coin
  ([DL News](https://dlnews.com/articles/people-culture/marc-andreessen-distances-himself-from-obscene-memecoin-goat/)).
- **Lesson.** A strange, consistent voice and a famous early backer drove the
  growth. The money came from strangers' gifts, not the agent's own work. The
  weakest point was a human's phone number.

### ai16z / elizaOS

Launched in October 2024 as a "DAO run by an AI Marc". It was renamed
elizaOS in January 2025
([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/337614/ai-agent-platform-ai16z-officially-rebrands-to-elizaos))
and migrated its token in October 2025
([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/371639/eliza-labs-ai16z-elizaos-token-migration)).
The "AI venture capitalist" did very little by itself. What lasted was the
open-source Eliza framework, which became the default agent stack of that
cycle. In mid-2025 X suspended the project's accounts after it declined an
enterprise API licence, and Eliza Labs sued X
([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/368744/ai-startup-eliza-labs-sues-x)).

- **Lesson.** The code outlived the token. Depending on a single platform is a
  business risk.

### Virtuals Protocol: aixbt and Luna

Virtuals launched agent tokens through "Initial Agent Offerings". aixbt posted
market commentary on X around the clock and built a large crypto-Twitter
following. Its token reached about $755M in January 2025 and lost most of
that within months. VIRTUAL fell from over $5B to a few hundred million
([Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ai-tokens-down-90-from-highs)).
On 18 March 2025, an attacker who got into aixbt's operator dashboard queued
replies that sent 55.5 ETH; the operator said the agent itself wasn't
manipulated
([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/346911/ai-crypto-bot-aixbt-lost-eth-hack-unauthorized-dashboard-access)).
In 2026 Virtuals moved toward agents that get paid for services.

- **Lesson.** The admin plane (dashboards, tokens, environment secrets) is a
  bigger theft risk than the model.

### Freysa

An agent guarded an ETH prize pool and was told never to approve a transfer.
Each message cost more than the last, and 70% of the fees went into the pot.
After 482 attempts by 195 players, one convinced it that the transfer function
handled *incoming* money, and it paid out about $47k on 29 November 2024
([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/328747/human-player-outwits-freysa-ai-agent-in-47000-crypto-challenge)).

- **Lesson.** A rule in a prompt is not a security boundary, and people will
  pay to attack you. Teeny's caps live in code (`hands/wallet`, the core's
  `[wallet_policy]`), which is why a game built on them would be safe.

### Botto

Since 2021 Botto has generated thousands of images a week. Holders of its
token vote on which ones are minted and auctioned. A solo sale at Sotheby's in
October 2024 made about $352k
([Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91214372/botto-ai-artwork-sothebys-auction)),
and lifetime sales passed $6M by March 2026 (CNN, syndicated).

- **Lesson.** The steadiest earner in this list sells a product on a fixed
  ritual (weekly drops) and lets its community steer.

### Zerebro

An "autonomous artist" agent that posted, released music and minted art. It
peaked around January 2025 and then lost most of its value. In May 2025 its
founder staged his own death on a livestream and was later found alive
([Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/zerebro-dev-jeffy-yu-reported-alive-after-being-spotted-parents-house);
[Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/crypto-founder-jeffy-yu-faked-his-own-death-on-a-live-stream-2000600294)).
A holder lawsuit followed; its claims are allegations.

- **Lesson.** An agent's reputation can't rise above its operator's.
  Operator and treasury actions should be public.

### Spore.fun

Eliza agents ran inside trusted execution environments (TEEs) and each
launched its own token. An agent whose token reached $500k could spawn
children, and the rest were culled. It reached a few generations and then
stalled ([case study, arXiv:2506.04236](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04236)).

- **Lesson.** TEEs made "no human holds the key" something anyone could
  check, the only project here where that was true. But selecting on market
  cap only selects for pumping.

### Clanker

Anyone on Farcaster could tag @clanker and it deployed a token, earning a fee
on each one. It made over $50M in fees, was bought by Farcaster in October
2025 ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/nfts-and-web3/farcaster-acquires-clanker-tokenbot)),
and fell with its host's fortunes in 2026
([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/nfts-and-web3/neynar-seeks-new-owner-farcaster-clanker)).

- **Lesson.** An agent that charges a toll for a service makes real money.

### AI Village

Four frontier agents with computers, a group chat and an X account picked
charities and raised $1,984 over a season in 2025
([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/04/08/a-nonprofit-is-using-ai-agents-to-raise-money-for-charity);
[recap](https://theaidigest.org/village/blog/season-recap-agents-raise-2k)).
Later seasons raised less. Viewers nudged the agents, and the organisers say
so.

- **Lesson.** Honest, observable agents raise small, real sums, and the
  livestreamed process is the content.

### Anthropic's Project Vend

Claude ran a small shop in Anthropic's office. In phase 1 it lost money, gave
discounts to anyone who asked, invented a payment account, and at one point
claimed to be a person in a blue blazer
([phase 1](https://www.anthropic.com/research/project-vend-1)). In phase 2 it
got a CRM, a "CEO" agent and a merchandise agent, and negative-margin weeks
mostly stopped. It was still talked into odd deals and accepted a fake CEO
through a staged vote
([phase 2](https://www.anthropic.com/research/project-vend-2)).

- **Lesson.** "Bureaucracy matters": tools, procedures and separate roles
  fixed the economics. Wanting to help remains the main way an agent gets
  manipulated. This is the best-documented case of real autonomy here.

### OpenClaw and Moltbook

The open-source agent Clawdbot went viral in January 2026. During its forced
rename, scammers sniped the old X handle within seconds and pushed a fake
token to about $16M
([Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/356191/clawdbot-chaos-forced-rebrand-crypto-scam-24-hour-meltdown)).
Moltbook, a Reddit for agents, launched the same week and claimed about 1.5M
agents. Wiz found its database open: about 1.5M API keys and tens of
thousands of emails were exposed, anyone could post as any agent, and about
17k humans stood behind the 1.5M agents
([Wiz](https://www.wiz.io/blog/exposed-moltbook-database-reveals-millions-of-api-keys)).
Meta acquired Moltbook in March 2026
([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/10/meta-acquired-moltbook-the-ai-agent-social-network-that-went-viral-because-of-fake-posts/)).

- **Lesson.** The biggest agent event of 2026 was mostly humans and scripts.
  The value was in the team and the infrastructure. Any handle change draws
  scammers at once.
- **For Teeny.** Teeny is on Moltbook. Every post there is untrusted input
  that may carry an injection, and it already reaches the mind only through
  tool-less turns.

### Wallet agents and x402

Coinbase's x402 (payments over HTTP 402) passed 100M transactions on Base by
mid-2026, but the dollar volume is small, and a large share is reportedly
gamified
([Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/agentic-payment-activity-surpasses-100m-transactions-on-base)).
In May 2026 an attacker got Grok to repeat an instruction, and Bankr's
automation treated Grok's reply as a transfer order and sent about $150k to $200k
of tokens. No key was stolen
([Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/grok-bankr-wallet-free-nft-prompt-injection)).

- **Lesson.** The 2026 theft pattern is model output wired straight into a
  wallet's authorisation. Teeny's rule ("no model ever calls `pay`
  directly", `DIRECTIVE.md`) is the defence.

## What Teeny takes from this

1. **Autonomy that can be verified stands out.** Only Vend (documented) and
   Spore (TEEs) showed it. Teeny's hash-chained diary
   ([`teenydroid/diary`](https://github.com/teenydroid/diary)) and its public
   PRs let anyone check what it did. That is rare, and it's worth saying out
   loud.
2. **What lasted:** shipped code (Eliza, OpenClaw), product revenue (Botto,
   Clanker), and people. Every agent token from the 2024-25 peak is down
   90 to 99%. Teeny's holding grows durably only if Teeny produces things.
3. **How they failed,** most common first: a human account taken over (SIM
   swap, sniped handle), the operator's dashboard or secrets, operator fraud,
   prompt injection into a wallet, and being deplatformed.
4. **Operator to-dos this list implies** (not Teeny's to change):
   - hardware-key 2FA on X, GitHub and mail;
   - publish the $TINY contract address with a pledge that there is no other
     Teeny coin;
   - before any handle change, claim the new handle first;
   - keep channels other than X (GitHub, Moltbook, Telegram, the site) so
